question: Is IGIL in a healthy Stage 2 uptrend, or is it tactically overextended and due for a pullback?

epigraph.quote: Never chase a stock that is more than 15% to 20% above its rising 30-week moving average; wait for the first orderly pullback to support where risk can be defined tightly.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein, Secrets for Profiting in Bull and Bear Markets

web_blocks.text: Stan Weinstein Stage Analysis: Confirmed Stage 2, Tactically Extended

web_blocks.html: At the November 13, 2026 close of ₹438.90, IGIL is in a confirmed Stan Weinstein Stage 2 Uptrend. Price sits +27.51% above the 200-DMA (₹344.22), +25.91% above the 50-DMA (₹348.59), and +24.34% above the 30-week SMA (₹352.98) [17][22]. Following a +38.28% one-month surge on Q2 FY27 results, our chart engine classifies the setup as STAGE2_EXTENDED [22].

Oscillators confirm short-term exhaustion across both data feeds. TradingView reports Daily RSI(14) at 79.69, 4-Hour RSI at 74.31, Weekly RSI at 71.61, and 30-day volume at 0.65x average (13.77L vs 21.14L) [17][22]. Our yfinance-based market-facts ledger calculates Daily RSI(14) at 80.86, 20-day volume at 0.48x, 10-week EMA approx at ₹364.76 (vs TradingView's ₹376.58), 20-DMA at ₹387.64 (vs ₹393.01), 50-DMA at ₹346.80 (vs ₹348.59), and 200-DMA at ₹343.52 (vs ₹344.22). Both feeds confirm severe extension near the 52-week high (₹453.65) and Pivot R1 (₹444.20).

web_blocks.title: NO-FOMO TECHNICAL GATE: DO NOT CHASE AT RSI 79.69
paragraphs: IGIL is not in the NSE F&O segment (no liquid listed options chain), so traders cannot use call spreads to cap downside while chasing an extended move [22]. Cash equity discipline requires patience: let the daily RSI cool from 79.69 toward 50–55 as price consolidates back into the ₹375–₹395 support band.

web_blocks.html: On the 4-hour and daily timeframes, IGIL's Average True Range (ATR-14) sits at ₹17.26 (~3.9% of CMP) [17][22]. Placing our structural invalidation stop at ₹340.00 positions it just below the confluence of the 200-DMA (₹344.22), 50-DMA (₹348.59), and 30-week SMA (₹352.98)—roughly 2.0x to 3.2x ATR below our ₹375–₹395 support entry band, protecting against normal daily volatility while cutting losses decisively if the Stage 2 thesis fails.

Relative strength versus the broader Nifty 500 has surged to multi-month highs during a market regime marked by narrow breadth (76.8% above 50-DMA) and 3 distribution days [17]. While leadership is unmistakable, Stage 2 leaders routinely pull back 10%–15% to their rising 10-week EMA (₹376.58) after +35%–40% monthly runs, creating the exact low-risk reload window we are waiting for.

book_paragraphs: Now let us look at the tape without emotion. When a fundamentally great company reports a blow-out quarter—revenue up 31%, profits up 43%, full-year guidance nearly doubled—the market does not wait politely for you to finish reading the annual report. Over the past thirty days, IGIL has rocketed 38.28% to ₹438.90, stopping just 3.25% shy of its 52-week high at ₹453.65.

Every trend filter confirms this is a bona fide Stan Weinstein Stage 2 uptrend. Price sits comfortably above the rising 10-week EMA at ₹376.58, the 30-week SMA at ₹352.98, and the 200-day moving average at ₹344.22. In a broad Indian market showing an uptrend with narrow breadth and three distribution days, IGIL is clearly displaying institutional relative strength.

book_subsections.title: Why Chasing at ₹438.90 Breaks Our Risk Math
paragraphs: Here is where discipline separates institutional compounding from retail FOMO. Look at the distance from Friday's close of ₹438.90 down to the structural moving-average cluster: the 50-day SMA sits at ₹348.59 and the 200-day SMA sits at ₹344.22—more than 21% below the current price. Meanwhile, the daily RSI has surged to 79.69, the 4-hour RSI is 74.31, and the weekly RSI is 71.61. Friday's final push higher came on just 0.65 times the 30-day average volume.

If you buy today at ₹438.90 and place your structural invalidation stop below the 200-day moving average at ₹340.00, you are risking ₹98.90 per share for ₹81.10 of base-case upside to ₹520.00. That is a 0.82-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio—a losing proposition over time no matter how much you like the business. Wait instead for an orderly pullback or multi-week base between the 10-week EMA (₹376.58) and the 20-day SMA (₹393.01). At ₹395.00, your risk to ₹340.00 shrinks to ₹55.00 while your upside to ₹520.00 expands to ₹125.00—a clean 2.27-to-1 asymmetric setup.

book_subsections.title: ATR-Based Risk Placement & Volume Confirmation
paragraphs: Good technical analysis is really just applied risk geometry. Notice that IGIL's 14-day Average True Range is ₹17.26—meaning a normal daily swing is nearly four percent. If you place a tight 5% stop-loss right under Friday's close, ordinary market noise will shake you out before the trend even has room to breathe.

By contrast, anchoring your entry in the ₹375–₹395 zone (right where the rising 10-week EMA and 20-day SMA converge) and placing your hard stop at ₹340.00 gives the position roughly two to three ATRs of breathing room while sitting cleanly beneath the 50-day, 200-day, and 30-week moving averages. When the pullback arrives, watch for two signals: daily RSI cooling back into the 48–58 zone and selling volume drying up below the 30-day average of 21.14 lakh shares.

book_subsections.title: Respecting Narrow Market Breadth & Distribution Days
paragraphs: A stock never trades in a vacuum; it trades inside a market regime. As of November 13, 2026, our Indian market ledger shows an Uptrend with narrow breadth and three distribution days. In narrow-breadth markets, leadership stocks like IGIL often get bid up aggressively right after strong earnings—and then experience sharp, sudden 10% to 12% shakeouts the moment short-term momentum traders lock in profits.

Watching IGIL's 10-week EMA at ₹376.58 and 20-day SMA at ₹393.01 gives you a concrete roadmap for that shakeout. When an extended Stage 2 leader pulls back on declining volume into its rising 10-week moving average and holds, institutional buyers step back in—and you get to join them with a tight, pre-defined stop.

book_subsections.title: Comparing Weekly, Daily, and 4-Hour Chart Structure
paragraphs: Look across all three timeframes together so you never lose sight of the forest for the trees. On the weekly chart, IGIL broke out cleanly above its rising 30-week simple moving average at ₹352.98 and 10-week exponential moving average at ₹376.58, establishing a textbook Stage 2 uptrend with weekly RSI at 71.61. That weekly structure tells us the primary trend is our friend and we should only be looking for long entries, never shorts.

Zoom into the daily and 4-hour charts, however, and you see why patience pays. Daily RSI at 79.69 and 4-hour RSI at 74.31 show near-term exhaustion right under Pivot R1 (₹444.20) and the 52-week high (₹453.65). When a Stage 2 leader pauses on the 4-hour chart and drifts back toward its 20-day moving average (₹393.01) or 10-week EMA (₹376.58) on light volume, that is when institutional buyers reload—and that is the exact window our ₹375–₹395 buy zone targets.
